learningObjectives: Create an image-based control using Advanced Identification in XScan.
Evaluate image identification against alternative methods and its execution-environment constraints.
Apply the multi-screenshot technique for controls that do not always look the same.
Distinguish XScan anchor algorithms from PDF-specific anchor requirements.

elements.term: Identifying by what it looks like
elements.description: XScan can pair a selected control with one or more screenshot identifiers. Image matching provides appearance-based identification when that fits the target, but still requires a visible, sufficiently distinctive identifier.

In XScan Advanced View, select the control and choose ADVANCED IDENTIFICATION → IMAGE. Add an identifier image, capture its region and inspect uniqueness. Set Accuracy and choose Method Fullscreen, Controlbased or Auto as appropriate.

elements.text: Evaluate properties, index and anchors alongside image identification. The current public image guide describes alternatives rather than prescribing a universal five-step order. Image matching is sensitive to design, resolution, color depth and scrolling; structural identification can also fail after UI changes.

bulletPoints: Select a control in XScan Advanced View, add image identifiers and check their uniqueness.
Validate the chosen Accuracy and search Method under the intended execution settings.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Making image identification as reliable as it can be

elements.description: Capture necessary variants when a control’s appearance changes. Tosca tries identifiers sequentially until it finds a match, so additional images increase execution time. Limit them to what is needed, and verify that each identifier selects the intended control.

Keep scan and execution display settings consistent. Multiple identifiers can cover known variants; they do not guarantee tolerance of arbitrary redesigns, scaling or rendering changes. A non-unique identifier remains unreliable even if Module creation is permitted.

bulletPoints: Use necessary appearance variants; adding screenshots increases search time.
Check visible identifiers for uniqueness and validate the execution environment.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The other Advanced Identification method: Anchor

elements.description: In XScan Advanced View, select the target and choose ADVANCED IDENTIFICATION → ANCHOR. Assign a reference control from the tree, screen or Auto Select. This establishes an anchor context for locating the target; it is not the PDF Scan’s text/image/same-page rule set.

elements.title: XScan Relative Algorithm choices
items: ShortestPath — searches from the anchor’s children and expands through tree levels toward the root.
Coordinate — uses anchor coordinates to define the search angle.
Auto — the default; tries ShortestPath and falls back to Coordinate.

elements.text: PDF and XScan anchors share the idea of a reference but have different documented identification mechanisms. Do not transfer the PDF-specific three conditions into a universal XScan rule.

bulletPoints: Assign an anchor and inspect its identification properties.
Relative Algorithm choices: ShortestPath, Coordinate, Auto (default).

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Where this sits in the escalation path

elements.title: Independent method-selection guidance
items: Evaluate supported properties and index selection.
Consider an anchor that provides useful, identifiable context.
Evaluate supported alternative engines or compatible adapters when applicable.
Use image identification when its appearance and environment assumptions fit, and test uniqueness and search cost.

elements.text: Self-healing is an execution-time recovery feature for documented supported engines. The support list alone does not establish that every identification mode is covered. Validate the actual control/engine combination; do not assume that it will repair an image mismatch.
📄 Official Tricentis Academy exercise material for this lesson is not redistributed here — complete the exercises inside the official course.

bulletPoints: Choose and validate a method for the actual control; the sequence is independent guidance, not an official universal ranking.

examPitfalls.title: Using image-based identification as a first resort
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Switching to IMAGE identification as soon as a control is awkward to identify by properties, because it is quick to set up.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Evaluate supported properties, index, anchors and relevant alternatives before committing to appearance matching. This is an engineering choice; the current guide does not establish a mandatory five-step order.

examPitfalls.title: Supplying a single screenshot for a control with several visual states
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Capturing one image of a button and finding the TestCase fails intermittently when the button is hovered or focused.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Capture necessary known variants, inspect uniqueness and verify execution. Extra screenshots add search time and do not themselves guarantee a correct match.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming image-based controls port cleanly between machines
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Authoring image-based controls on a high-DPI laptop and deploying to execution agents with different display settings.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Keep scan and execution display settings consistent and test the actual environments. Known image variants are not a guarantee against every environment change.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing anchor identification with image identification
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating ANCHOR and IMAGE as the same fallback because they sit next to each other under Advanced Identification.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: XScan anchors use reference context with ShortestPath, Coordinate or Auto. Image identification searches screenshot identifiers. PDF-specific text/image/same-page conditions are not a universal XScan rule.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting self-healing to rescue an image-based control
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Enabling the SelfHealing TCP and assuming image-identified controls are now resilient too.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Do not infer image-mode support from an engine’s general self-healing support. Check the actual combination and investigate failed image matches, including uniqueness, appearance and search settings.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When is it reasonable to evaluate image-based identification?

options.text: Whenever it is faster to set up than property-based identification.
When other supported identification methods are unsuitable and its visual/environment assumptions can be validated.
For every control in a Windows desktop application.
Only for controls inside PDF documents.

practiceQuiz.hint: Check whether the method’s assumptions fit the target.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Image identification is a possible choice alongside properties, index and anchors. Validate known appearance, uniqueness and execution settings rather than treating convenience as sufficient.

optionExplanations.A: Setup speed alone does not validate identifier uniqueness or execution constraints.
optionExplanations.B: Evaluate alternatives and verify that appearance and environment assumptions fit the target.
optionExplanations.C: The method is not mandated for all Windows controls.
optionExplanations.D: XScan image identification is not limited to PDF document controls.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A button changes appearance between its default, hovered and focused states, and the image-based control matches only sometimes. What is the recommended fix?

options.text: Lower the match accuracy until all states pass.
Supply more than one screenshot, covering the control's different appearances.
Switch the Module to a different engine.
Take the screenshot at a higher resolution.

practiceQuiz.hint: The documented technique addresses controls that don't always look the same.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Multiple necessary reference images can cover known visual states. Tosca searches sequentially, so test uniqueness and accuracy and account for additional execution time; success is not guaranteed merely by adding images.

optionExplanations.A: Broadly weakening accuracy can accept an unintended identifier instead of representing known states.
optionExplanations.B: Necessary images can cover known variants, with uniqueness checks and additional search cost.
optionExplanations.C: An engine change alone does not address these stated screenshot variants.
optionExplanations.D: A higher-resolution capture does not by itself cover different visual states.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where in XScan do you configure image-based identification for a control?

options.text: In the Module's Self-Healing Properties tab.
In the Identification methods pane: ADVANCED IDENTIFICATION → IMAGE.
In Project Settings → Engines.
By right-clicking the application tile during the scan.

practiceQuiz.hint: It lives next to the ANCHOR option.
practiceQuiz.rationale: You select the control and then choose ADVANCED IDENTIFICATION → IMAGE in the Identification methods pane. ANCHOR is the sibling option in the same pane.

optionExplanations.A: Self-Healing Properties is not the identifier image configuration pane.
optionExplanations.B: Advanced View’s IMAGE pane configures screenshot identifiers and their search properties.
optionExplanations.C: This is a selected control’s identification workflow, not the stated project setting.
optionExplanations.D: The application tile chooses scan technology rather than configuring this selected control’s images.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Relative Algorithm choices does the on-prem XScan anchor reference list? (three correct answers)

options.text: ShortestPath
Coordinate
Auto
ByteCompare

practiceQuiz.hint: Auto combines the two explicit search algorithms.
practiceQuiz.rationale: XScan lists ShortestPath and Coordinate, with Auto as the default that tries ShortestPath before Coordinate. These are distinct from PDF anchor requirements.

optionExplanations.A: ShortestPath is a documented Relative Algorithm.
optionExplanations.B: Coordinate is a documented Relative Algorithm.
optionExplanations.C: Auto is the default, using ShortestPath then Coordinate fallback.
optionExplanations.D: ByteCompare is not one of the listed XScan anchor Relative Algorithms.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A target lacks unique properties but has a distinctive nearby reference control. What can be evaluated before using screenshot matching?

options.text: Anchor-based identification, using the label as the anchor control.
Nothing — image-based is the only remaining option.
Enable self-healing and rerun.
Delete and rescan the whole application.

practiceQuiz.hint: A unique neighbour on the same page is exactly what one method is designed to exploit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A useful reference control can support XScan anchor identification. Evaluate the Relative Algorithm and verify the target; a nearby label alone is not a guarantee that identification will work.

optionExplanations.A: A suitable reference label can be evaluated as an XScan anchor.
optionExplanations.B: The target’s missing properties do not eliminate reference-based identification.
optionExplanations.C: Self-healing alone does not define the missing target’s suitable identification method.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting the whole application model is not required to evaluate a local anchor.

quickRecap.value: Image-Based Test Automation — identifies a control by one or more screenshots instead of by structure.
XScan → select control → Identification methods pane → ADVANCED IDENTIFICATION → IMAGE.
Evaluate image matching alongside properties, index and anchors; no mandatory universal ranking is asserted.
Use more than one screenshot, especially when the control doesn't always look the same.
Design, resolution, color depth, scrolling and rendering changes can affect matching; structural methods also require validation.
XScan reference context with ShortestPath, Coordinate or Auto; do not substitute PDF-specific rules.
Independent guidance: assess supported alternatives, environment assumptions, uniqueness and search cost.
Check the actual engine/identification combination; do not assume recovery of an image mismatch.
